Today, Amazon's Ring subsidiary announced its first smart door lock. It addresses a major issue that has plagued many smart lock users: dead batteries. Ring has an clever solution to this problem and will launch it in the first quarter of 2027. Additionally, the company unveiled several new security cameras with improved low-light performance.

Ring 智能門鎖

The concept of a smart lock isn't new, but Ring aims to solve the dead battery problem. To prevent you from being locked out at an inconvenient time, the Ring smart lock lets you turn a manual dial a few times to generate enough power to temporarily power the lock, allowing you to open the door and get back inside.

The Ring smart lock supports all the features you'd want from a smart lock. You can unlock it using your fingerprint, a touch keypad, or your phone with the Ring app.

The Ring app also enables several features, including remote viewing and locking, or setting up scheduled or timed unlocks for family members or other visitors. It also integrates with Amazon Echo and any other Ring doorbells and cameras you may have.

The lock comes in three finishes: black, silver, and brass, and requires no additional wiring for installation. It will go on sale early next year for $249. You can learn more details here.

New 4K Cameras

From Jason's top comment

If only there was a way to not need power and just manually unlock it... 🤔

In addition to its first smart lock, Ring also unveiled several new 4K cameras supporting the new Retinal Vision 4K standard. This means you get better low-light performance and more accurate color reproduction. All products are available for pre-order or purchase starting today:

  • Outdoor Cam 4K Plus: 140° ultra-wide field of view, with multiple power options including battery, plug-in, direct power, and Power over Ethernet (PoE) — $149.99 on Amazon, learn more here.
  • Floodlight Cam 4K Plus: powerful floodlight, supports 24/7 continuous recording and smart detection, requires direct power — $219.99 on Amazon, learn more here.
  • Spotlight Cam 4K Plus: 550-lumen spotlight, 140° ultra-wide field of view, available in battery, plug-in, and solar configurations — $199.99 on Amazon, learn more here.
  • Indoor Cam 4K: Ring's first 4K indoor camera, supports dual-band Wi-Fi 6, with a 115° field of view — $99.99 on Amazon, learn more here.

Ring also unveiled the new Pan-Tilt Indoor Cam 2K for $69.99, offering 360° pan coverage at a more affordable price. It can track motion and includes a privacy cover. You can learn more here.
